title: IO completion record
description: Language-neutral description of a completion event emitted by the I/O backend. Every submission eventually produces either exactly one completion record OR is dropped (when its epoch is stale — see io-submission.schema.json § 'epoch' and pager-async.spec.md § 'Cancellation semantics'). Fields other than user_data are populated per-op; see § 'Result interpretation' below.

user_data.description: Verbatim echo of the submission's user_data. The submitter uses this as the correlation key.

epoch.description: Verbatim echo of the submission's epoch. If the submitter's current epoch has advanced past this value, the submitter MUST drop this completion without raising an error.

outcome.description: Terminal status of the submission. 'ok' means success; 'error' means the backend raised one of the enumerated error conditions; 'cancelled' means the submission was cancelled (either by an explicit cancel op or by backend-initiated teardown on epoch advance).

result_bytes.description: For a successful read or write, the number of bytes transferred. MUST equal the submission's 'length' on success; a lower value MUST be reported as outcome='error' with error_condition='IO_BACKEND_SHORT_READ' or 'IO_BACKEND_SHORT_WRITE'. For open_read / open_write, this is the assigned handle identifier (to be stored by the submitter and used in subsequent submissions). For fsync / fsync_dir / close / rename / unlink / cancel, this field is absent or zero.

error_condition.description: Required when outcome == 'error'. Absent otherwise. See § 'Error conditions' in io-backend.spec.md for the complete enumeration.

reason.description: Optional human-readable diagnostic string. Generators MAY populate this with errno names, std::io::Error displays, or other native error text. Never consulted by callers for control flow; tests match against error_condition only.
